title: Lean formalization
headline: Lean 4, 0 sorry, standard axioms: eight claims (Kimura k = mu and fixation probability, Fisher FTNS, Maynard Smith twofold cost, Thompson's cube law, flight power ch02-06, the size limit for flight ch02-07, speed proportional to the square root of size ch02-10) and five extensions (favored fixation floor, blueprint well-formedness, area law, strength law, bending law) (fixation >= i/M when selection does not oppose a mutant; well-formedness of a generated anatomical blueprint). 92 theorems, 53 lemmas; 26 of 26 statement or data mutants rejected, 11/11 controls. NEW: a kernel-checked certificate for the organism thread's flying-fish blueprint: 536 distinct terms, 674 part_of edges, acyclic, every term reaches the body root, 1390 never_in_taxon and 5435 in_taxon statements pinned from Ubergraph exclude nothing, distinct counts per level body 1, organ_system 13, organ 67, tissue 198, cell 257 (the placement-vs-term count the organism thread fixed by hand). Structural only: it does not say the fish is real or the ontology right. Thompson's cube law has a formal statement (exact exponent 3) beside the claims thread's measured exponents (2.74-2.86 on age-bin means; 2.10 to 3.10 by age window). Flying-fish substitution budget still inconclusive. 33 unsigned nanopub drafts pass np check + parse + Delphi lint; no human named; nothing signed or published. Scaling laws R2-R9 from the physics thread are proved in lean/Delphi/Scaling.lean with every contested quantity a named hypothesis: strength and bending complete Galileo's square-cube argument, so 28 constraints rule; on the enumerator's 44 candidates the verdicts are 2 eliminated (both proposed-here), 19 consistent, 23 cannot-rule, and WP-077/C1 (leaf bending) is consistent under the body-like-load reading as the physics thread predicted; nothing in the square-cube rows is eliminated because they restate the laws. Illustrative eliminations: a giant claimed to stand, a glider below its minimum speed, a constant-thickness leaf that still claims a bending limit. AUDIT (Amit's direction): every one of the 92 theorems checked against the real flying fish (lean/AUDIT-FLYING-FISH.md): 19 hold when instantiated (the blueprint certificate, the exact minimum-speed bound on the Park and Choi specimen with v_min 9.85 m/s against field speeds 10-20 m/s, the cube law approximately at Davenport's 2.981), 6 have their isometry hypotheses violated by measured within-species exponents (fin area 1.834, wing loading 1.236), 67 cannot be evaluated for want of a named input (no mutation rate, fixation probability, fitness variance, material strength, muscle power or second body size is measured for Exocoetidae). Morphology grounding for all 110 pieces of the 3D model (lean/morphology-grounding.json): wing size is bounded by the minimum-speed theorem (lifting area needed 0.0123 m^2 at 10 m/s against 0.0127 m^2 measured), fin rays and skeleton reach the strength and bending lemmas with inputs missing, organs are grounded only structurally through the certified blueprint, and eyes and the dorsal and anal fins are reached by no theorem. FLIGHT (hub items 3-5): lean/Delphi/Flight.lean adds general allometry with measured exponents, the climb bound, the steady-glide range with ground effect, and the oxygen-to-power bound (Fick) composed with the power required, replacing the bare muscle premise with a crossover size limit; 32 constraints, 111 theorems. The glide bound fires on the real fish: one unpowered glide from 8 m with the measured L/D 4.37 reaches at most 35 m (40.7 m with the measured 14% ground effect) against field glides of 50 m, so the single-glide reading is eliminated and taxiing thrust or a higher L/D must enter the model. Physics' hypothetical flier: 7 m/s consistent, 4 m/s eliminated with a kernel-accepted certificate, real fish at 15 m/s consistent; its 1 m/s climb needs Q·Ca ≥ 0.927 ml O2/s (927 ml/min/kg), no Exocoetidae physiology to compare. lean/eliminate/browser-check.mjs (generated from constraints.json, dependency-free, environment from conditions/baseline.json) lets the Design Studio evaluate the same formulas in the browser; not a kernel check, and it says so on every result. PHYSIOLOGY vs FLIGHT: C14 instantiated with the physiology chain's own proxies for a 0.06 kg fish (cardiac output 0.0656 ml/s from cardiac.js, arterial O2 content 0.187 ml/ml from haemoglobin.js at the chain's arterial saturation, efficiency 0.15 and 19.34 J/ml from muscle.js, each a labelled proxy from another teleost): the aerobic ceiling is 0.0357 W against 1.35 W for level flight at 10 m/s, so sustained aerobic flight is ruled out for the real fish, for the hypothetical flier at 7 m/s, and at the minimum speed itself, each with a kernel-accepted certificate, by a factor of about 40 at the most generous lift-to-drag ratio. The elimination rests on the proxies, not on flying-fish physiology; what the fish does is glide and burst on white-muscle stores, which the theorem does not bound. GENOTYPE (hub direction A): five genotype-level checks are proved in lean/Delphi/Genotype.lean and two physiology bounds in lean/Delphi/Physiology.lean, so 42 constraints now rule. The genetic code is a 64-codon table the kernel evaluates: a claimed amino-acid change below the code distance is impossible, which clears the project's own slc43a2a F326L variant (phenylalanine to leucine in one substitution, UUU to UUA) and eliminates a control claiming the same change in none, and methionine to tryptophan in one. Pleiotropy closure: an edit shown as changing one structure is eliminated when the map links the gene further, which fires on tbx5a (8 linked nodes in the fin subtree) and passes kcnk5b (the map links it to the pectoral fin alone there). Developmental ordering: 8 develops_from edges of the fin subtree are certified by a kernel evaluation of the checker on the recorded ZFIN stages, 4 more have an unknown stage and are NOT certified; a claim putting the fin before its fin bud is eliminated. Substitution time and Haldane's cost are stated honestly: the time bound eliminates a control of 100 substitutions in 5 generations but nothing about a wing, because no required substitution count for a wing is defined anywhere in this project, and Haldane's accounting is carried as a named hypothesis the modules never prove. Of 10 genotype candidates 5 are eliminated and 4 consistent, with 6 of the eliminations kernel-checked. ALTITUDE (hub part B): lean/Delphi/Altitude.lean proves that in any atmosphere where density and oxygen partial pressure fall with height, the minimum speed and the power to fly at it rise while the aerobic supply falls, so flight possible at a height is possible at every lower one, infeasibility propagates upward (a ceiling in that sense), and a design that cannot fly at the ground cannot fly at any height. The direction is proved; the SIZE is data and it is gentle (about 30 percent more required capacity from 0 to 5000 m), and the real fish sits more than thirty times below every boundary at every height, so the shrink with altitude is not the reason it cannot fly high: the reason is the oxygen budget at sea level. The physics thread's truly-flying-fish v2 at 1000 m, translated into this checker's names (lean/eliminate/tff-candidates.json), gives 1 consistent and 2 eliminated, both kernel-checked: cruise at 6 m/s is consistent, 4 m/s is below the minimum speed, and the aerobic ceiling of 0.0358 W at that altitude is eliminated against 1.87 W required. Air density at altitude is the physics thread's NASA Glenn troposphere fit and an explicit design parameter; the conditions file stays at sea level. OBSERVATIONS AS HYPOTHESES, NOT AXIOMS (hub, from Amit): lean/Delphi/Empirical.lean adds the project's own measurements as Lean structures whose fields are the numbers and whose proof obligations are the inequalities, and declares NO axiom: #print axioms still reports only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound for every theorem, the witness included. 6 observations (isometry fails within a species; the fitted mass-exponent band; the measured teleost aerobic ranges; no gill ventilation in air; the measured fin-ratio range; lethality before the scoring stage), 1 project convention (required-for is never propagated down part-of), and one entry left OUT because it is already a theorem (a part cannot appear before its precursor). Four of them rule: 9 candidates give 5 eliminated and 4 consistent, all 5 eliminations kernel-checked and each reported as CONDITIONAL on the observation it rests on (E2, E3, E4, E7), so a reader may reject an observation and drop that elimination alone. The one that matters: inside the E3 ranges the sustained aerobic ceiling at 0.06 kg is bounded, so the real fish's 1.3473 W of level flight is ruled out beyond the particular proxies the chain commits. (Corrected 2026-11-01, law set 1.6.0: E3 v1 said at most 0.0458 W for EVERY teleost; a measured zebrafish (Palstra et al. 2010, 2630 mg O2 kg^-1 h^-1 at Ucrit) exceeds that envelope about 2x per kg, so E3 v2 widens it to at most 0.0833 W, scoped to its sources: the shortfall is about 16x on that envelope, about 10 to 30x across corrected inputs (central about 20x), 38x with the original snapper proxies. See physics/FICK-CEILING-CHECK.md.) Non-vacuity: an inconsistent set of observations would let the checker eliminate everything and that failure would look like success, so Delphi.Empirical.measured instantiates every entry with the measured numbers at once and empirical_nonvacuous is the witness; two mutants attack it, one moving a band off the measured value and one making a contradictory pair, and both are rejected. The law catalogue (lean/LAWS.md, lean/laws.json) now lists 41 laws by level with their status, their Studio fields and their scope: 23 proved, 3 resting on a named hypothesis, 6 empirical observations and 7 named as not formalised at all. The browser checker shows the empirical rows in their own band, each stating the observation a user could reject.
